![](thumbnail.png)

## Overview

This figure shows the household income distribution of students entering each higher-education sector, benchmarked not against the general population but against everyone who sat the same national college-entrance exam in that cohort. This lets it show whether a sector draws disproportionately from higher- or lower-income applicants relative to the pool of people actually competing for a seat, rather than only relative to society at large.

## Methodology

Income distribution of entrants (linked ENEM×Census records) by sector, benchmarked against the full pool of ENEM (Brazil's national high-school exam) examinees in the same cohort — i.e., against everyone who took the exam, not just those who enrolled. This lets the figure show whether a sector's entering class is income-skewed relative to the applicant pool it draws from, rather than only relative to the general population.

## Reproducibility

**Tier: B**

This pipeline depends on restricted INEP data accessible via SEDAP+ credentials (`SEDAP_TOKEN` environment variable). Without an approved credential, the scripts in `shared-pipeline/sedap/` will not run — the logic remains available for audit, but full reproduction requires requesting access.
